title: Addition and subtraction within 20
keyIdea: Within 20 you use strategies — make ten then add the rest, decompose a take-away so you hit ten first, count on from the larger number, and use related facts — not only snap recall of facts within 10.
familyTip: Ask: for 8 + 6, how many more make 8 into 10? Take those 2 from the 6, then add the leftover 4. Try the same break-to-ten idea with 13 − 5.

visual.caption: Within-20 strategy or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it then a box.

items: make ten then add the leftover
decompose a take-away to hit ten first
count on from the larger addend
within 20 means only partners that make 10

lab.caption: Flagship lab: fill toward ten, make-ten bridge for 8+6, decompose 13−5 to a ten, related take-away, count-on vs recount, catch stick-digits myth.

kid: Within 20 means sums and take-aways that stay between 0 and 20.
Make ten: for 8 + 6, take 2 from the 6 to fill 8 up to 10, then add the leftover 4 to get 14.
For take-away, break the number so you hit ten first — 13 − 5 becomes 13 − 3 = 10, then − 2 = 8.
You can also count on from the larger number, or use a related fact like 9 + 7 = 16 so 16 − 7 = 9.
adult: CCSS 1.OA.6: add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency within 10; use strategies such as counting on, making ten (e.g. 8 + 6 = 8 + 2 + 4), and decomposing a number leading to a ten (e.g. 13 − 4 = 13 − 3 − 1). Distinct from Fluent adding and subtracting within 10 (snap facts 0–10) and Number bonds within 20 (exact partner pairs).

Words: make ten, decompose, count on, related fact, within 20. Common mistakes: sticking digits (8 + 6 as 86); treating make-ten as stopping at 10; recounting every object from 1 instead of counting on.

In the lab your child fills a ten-frame toward 10, shows the make-ten bridge for 8 + 6, breaks 13 − 5 to a ten, uses a related take-away, picks count-on over recount, and spots the stick-digits mix-up.
